Wrap any element you want to float — images, videos, SVGs, cards — with `FloatingElement` and give it a `depth`: ```tsx import Floating, { FloatingElement } from "@/components/prsui/parallax-floating"; export function MyComponent() { return ( ); } ``` Elements with a higher `depth` travel further from the pointer, creating a parallax effect. The animation runs on `requestAnimationFrame` and eases each element toward its target, so it stays smooth even as elements are added or removed. Pointer tracking works with both mouse and touch. ## Props ### Floating | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Elements to float | | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes merged onto the wrapper | | `sensitivity` | `number` | `1` | Multiplier for how far elements travel | | `easingFactor` | `number` | `0.05` | Interpolation factor per frame toward the target (0-1)| ### FloatingElement | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ---------- | ------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The element that gets the floating effect | | `className`| `string` | - | Additional CSS classes merged onto the wrapper | | `depth` | `number` | `1` | How strongly this element reacts to the pointer |
